traits: Cap 3 to 7 cm, convex then dished into a funnel, often pierced at the centre onto the hollow stem; brown to tawny, greyish; margin rolled when young then wavy
No true gills underneath: grey or silvery-yellow folds, branched and forked near the edge, running down the stem
Stem 3 to 12 cm, bright yellow, long, thin, winding and hollow
In groups, often in lines, in broadleaf or mixed woods, on moss and litter, near very rotten wood · mid-autumn to the first frosts
safetyNote: A renowned edible, fresh or dried; it is on the German mycological society list (« Trompeten-Pfifferling ») and on the Swiss controllers’ list. It has edible look-alikes (Craterellus lutescens, C. melanoxeros); Leotia lubrica, gelatinous and said to be suspect, can grow alongside (Wikipedia FR).
